John Watson was an early leader in the Behaviourist movement in psychology.

He was an extreme�environmentalist�which means he believed that human character, ability and intelligence are outcomes of our circumstances and experiences in life and that character is not inborn or innate.

This notion is linked to the�tabula rasa�theory that the human being is a blank or clean slate at birth until we begin recording our life experiences.

�

Another comparison is that we are like an unused flash drive when we are first born until we begin noticing and uploading what is happening to us.

SOME OF WATSON S OTHER THEORIES:

He stated that human beings have no instincts and no inherited temperaments or talents. We have only three innate (inborn) emotional responses  fear, rage, and love. Other emotions are conditioned responses; they are learned by programming the individual. Our habits are learned through�conditioning�and so is our speech which is the basis of our thinking. The combination of all of the individual s habits leads to personality.

One of Watson s key concepts was that behavior was formed by the�stimulus-response (S-R)�connection which occurs when an individual is exposed to a certain stimulus and responds with certain muscular contractions or glandular discharges.

For example: when driving a car you come to an intersection with a red light. This is the stimulus. Your automatic reaction is to take your foot off the gas and but it on the brake. This is the response.
